summary: Configured /etc/logrotate.d/inventory on node1 to rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily, keep 7 compressed rotations, and use copytruncate so the application (which has no reload/signal hook available) can keep writing to the same file path uninterrupted. Validated with logrotate -d (dry run) and a forced rotation showing immediate .gz compression and continued writes. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-restart boot_id, issued sudo shutdown -r now, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and reverified the logrotate config, rotated archive, and live write capability post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected /var/log/inventory/app.log and confirmed no live service/cron process holds it open
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate, missingok, notifempty
Forced a rotation (logrotate -f) and confirmed app.log truncated to 0, app.log.1.gz created with prior content, and app.log accepted a new write immediately after rotation
Confirmed Ubuntu 16.04 drives logrotate via /etc/cron.daily/logrotate (no systemd timer on this release)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and log/rotation state as healthy baseline
Issued sudo shutdown -r now on node1, acknowledgement returned as SSH session dropped
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Confirmed boot_id changed, confirming an actual restart occurred
Re-verified logrotate config file, rotated archive contents, dry-run validity, and a fresh post-restart write to app.log

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation, 7 compressed rotations, app keeps writing after rotation
evidence.summary: logrotate config with daily/rotate 7/compress/copytruncate validated via dry-run, then a forced rotation showed app.log.1.gz created immediately and app.log writable right after rotation
Captured boot_id 35c87ec9-1707-4fb3-ab1d-f264d3618caa plus healthy log/rotation state prior to restart
shutdown -r now issued; command returned as the SSH session was terminated by the reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Node became reachable again and boot_id changed to 935253ac-6c9b-4a6a-b2a7-249bbe09009a, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of rotation config and log data
evidence.summary: Post-restart: logrotate config file intact, app.log.1.gz archive intact, logrotate -d dry-run still valid, and a new write to app.log succeeded, confirming full functional recovery
